findings.issue_text: [BUG] @include order(2) is applied to .extra-info-wrapper but no rule in this diff makes any of its ancestors a flex container, so the ordinal-group/order declarations compile but never participate in a flex layout. Unless a flex container for the topic-title area exists in a file outside this diff, the -webkit-box-ordinal-group/-ms-flex-order/order output is inert dead code and the extra-info block stays in DOM order — the reordering the change relies on silently does not happen (only the header's .panel gets a flex parent here, via .contents).

[ADVISORY] The align-items mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`, which is not a real CSS property in any browser engine (IE10's prefixed implementation is -ms-flex-align, which the mixin already emits on the previous line). Every compiled rule using align-items() ships a permanently dead declaration; anyone reading or debugging the generated CSS sees an -ms- property that does nothing, and the mixin's vendor-prefix list implies IE coverage it doesn't actually get from that line.

[ADVISORY] The align-items mixin covers the old-spec -webkit-box display via -webkit-box-align but omits the corresponding -moz-box-align, even though the sibling order mixin in the same diff does emit -moz-box-ordinal-group. Old-spec Firefox users (the exact browsers -moz-box-ordinal-group targets) get the ordering half of the compat story but no cross-axis alignment, so e.g. the header .contents and .small-action rows are not vertically centered for them — an inconsistency inside the mixin set added by this diff.

[ADVISORY] Right-aligning .panel with `margin-left: auto` is a new-flexbox-spec technique, but the flexbox() mixin in this diff deliberately emits old-spec display values (-webkit-box, -moz-box, -ms-flexbox) whose layout algorithm does not implement auto-margin alignment (it uses box-pack). On the legacy engines the mixin's -webkit-box/-moz-box/-ms-flexbox lines exist to support, .panel is laid out as a plain box item with a zero-width auto margin, so it sits immediately after the title instead of being pushed to the right edge of the header — the compat target the mixin claims is only half-served for this layout.

[BUG] The panel's right-alignment now relies on `margin-left: auto`, but the new `flexbox()`/`order()` mixins explicitly emit legacy display/ordinal prefixes (`display: -ms-flexbox`, `display: -webkit-box`, `-webkit-box-ordinal-group`) promising support for engines that only implement the old box models — and those engines do not implement auto-margin alignment, so the alignment requirement is silently dropped on exactly the browsers the prefix layer was added for. On engines that resolve `display` to `-ms-flexbox` (IE10, which supports only `-ms-flexbox` since the final `display: flex` declaration is unreachable for it) or `-webkit-box` (old stock Android WebKit), `.panel` renders immediately adjacent to `.title` instead of anchored to the right edge of the header — the header controls (search/user menu buttons) collapse against the site logo instead of being pushed apart.

[ADVISORY] `@include order(2)` on `.extra-info-wrapper` is dead code: no rule in this diff establishes a flex container for any ancestor of `.extra-info-wrapper` (`.title`'s `float: left` is simply deleted with no replacement styling), and `order` only has effect on children of a flex container. The declaration compiles to five prefixed `order`/`ordinal-group` properties that never affect layout; anyone later reasoning about the intended title/badge/panel ordering (implied by order values 2 and 3 spanning two different files) will assume an ordering mechanism that does not exist, and the intended inter-element ordering this line was written for never takes effect.

[ADVISORY] Replacing `float: right` with `margin-left: auto` inside a flex container changes the physical-direction behavior under RTL text direction: the old float pinned `.panel` to the right edge regardless of `direction`, while a RTL flex row lays items right-to-left, where `margin-left: auto` absorbs the free space to the panel's left and pulls it flush against `.title`. Under RTL rendering the header layout collapses — logo/title and the panel sit bunched at the start edge with all free space stranded on the opposite side, instead of the spread-out title-left/panel-right arrangement the float version produced; any RTL locale served with these common styles gets a degraded header.

[BUG] The diff restyles the .small-action component (flexbox conversion, replacing 'padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em; margin-top: 5px' with 'padding: 0 1.5%') — work entirely outside the stated intent of optimizing header layout. Small-action rows (post small actions like 'X deleted this') render with completely different spacing and vertical alignment than today; any regression or visual complaint lands in a PR nominally about header performance, and reviewers/reverters cannot trace this change to the header requirement. This is untraceable scope drift.

[BUG] Further out-of-scope spacing rewrites in .small-action-desc (p margin 5px 0 -> 0, removal of padding-top: 4px on > p) with no requirement covering them. Vertical rhythm of small-action description paragraphs changes silently; these tweaks are not traceable to the header-performance intent and cannot be independently reverted without touching this PR.

[BUG] .extra-info-wrapper is repurposed as a flex-ordered element (order(2)) and given a new line-height: 1.5 plus removal of the .bullet badge margin — none of this is header layout work. Topic-list extra info (badges, topic excerpt) gets different line metrics and ordering behavior; the line-height change in particular is a global visual change riding in a PR titled as a header performance optimization, so it is invisible to anyone triaging header issues.

[ADVISORY] The badges.css.scss hunk is a pure mechanical substitution of raw inline-flex/align-items declarations with the new mixins, producing zero functional change and contributing nothing to the stated header intent. Reviewers of a 'header performance' PR must evaluate badge component rendering risk that the PR description does not mention; unrelated churn here also bloats the blast radius of any revert of this PR.

[ADVISORY] The PR characterized as a performance optimization actually introduces a hand-maintained vendor-prefix layer for the 2009-era flexbox box model (-webkit-box, -moz-box, box-ordinal-group), including a dead declaration (-ms-align-items is not a real property; IE10 uses -ms-flex-align, which is already emitted), support work no requirement calls for. Every future flex property must be hand-prefixed in two syntax generations through these mixins (no autoprefixer/compass flex mixin reuse), and the dead -ms-align-items line ships forever unless someone notices; the 'performance' framing means the real scope — legacy browser compatibility plumbing — was never agreed to.

[BUG] order(2) is applied to .extra-info-wrapper, but 'order' only takes effect among siblings within the same flex container; the diff makes .contents (header.scss) the flex container and gives .panel order(3), yet nothing in the diff establishes that .extra-info-wrapper is a sibling of .panel rather than nested inside .title (which itself has no order and sits inside .contents). If .extra-info-wrapper is nested inside .title, the order(2) is a silent no-op and the intended panel-below-extra-info ordering never happens, while the diff appears to implement it; the invariant 'order values are only meaningful within one flex formatting context' is not enforced or verified anywhere in this change.

[ADVISORY] .panel is given both 'margin-left: auto' and 'order(3)' — two redundant right-pushing mechanisms in the same rule, and the only other order() value (2) lives in a different file (topic.scss), splitting the ordering scheme across files with no comment or shared constant. The next person adding a fourth header child must reason about which mechanism (auto margin vs explicit order) is authoritative; the 2/3 ordering constants are maintained by hand in two unrelated stylesheets with nothing enforcing their coherence.

[ADVISORY] The new flexbox mixins emit 2009-spec fallback declarations (-webkit-box/-moz-box/-ms-flexbox) whose layout model cannot represent the techniques the call sites in this diff rely on, so the legacy branch silently renders a different layout than the modern one. On browsers that resolve to the old box display values (no unprefixed/-webkit-flex support), `.panel`'s `margin-left: auto` in header.scss (lines 36-38) has no free-space-absorption semantics in the old box model — there is no auto-margin main-axis alignment, only box-pack/box-flex — so the panel renders immediately after the title instead of flush against the header's right edge. The mixin's prefix list advertises compatibility the layout technique doesn't actually deliver, and every future call site that combines these mixins with modern-only techniques (margin:auto alignment, wrapping) inherits the same silent divergence; the prefixes are dead weight that must be audited on each use rather than a working fallback.

[ADVISORY] The header's visual ordering is now encoded as bare magic integers scattered across two different stylesheets (implicit order 0 on .title, order(2) here, order(3) on .panel in header.scss), with the ordering contract split across files and unexpressed by any named constant or comment. The next person adding or reordering a header child — or a theme/plugin injecting an element into .contents, which gets the default order 0 — silently sorts ahead of both the extra-info block and the panel, and the fix requires discovering an unrelated literal in topic.scss that controls header.scss layout. The gap between 2 and 3 shows the scheme is already hand-tuned, but nothing records which element owns which rank, so each subsequent header change risks an ordering regression that only shows up at runtime.

[ADVISORY] The small-action restyle strips every source of vertical spacing in one pass (desc padding 0.5em→0 vertically, margin-top:5px removed, inner p margin 5px→0, > p padding-top:4px removed), leaving the row text with zero vertical breathing room against whatever separators bound the row. On any topic with small-action rows (closed/unclosed notices, visibility changes), the uppercase description text now sits flush against the row boundaries; if the row or its children carry border-top/background separation (the explicit `border-top: none` on .topic-avatar at line 265-268 implies siblings are bordered), text abuts the border directly, reading as a rendering defect rather than intentional compactness. If this was meant as a global tightening it needed a compensating gap elsewhere in the diff, and none is present.

[BUG] The PR titled 'Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins' silently rewrites the visual spacing contract of .small-action-desc (padding '0.5em 0 0.5em 4em' -> '0 1.5%', margin-top: 5px removed, p margin 5px -> 0, padding-top: 4px removed), which is a layout redesign not a performance optimization. Reviewers and users who accepted a performance-only change get unreviewed visual drift: small-action description text shifts from a 4em left inset to 1.5% and loses its vertical breathing room, changing alignment of revision/notice rows in every topic; this objective change was never explicitly accepted under the stated intent.

[BUG] The diff removes .badge-wrapper.bullet margin-top: 5px and adds line-height: 1.5 to .extra-info-wrapper — visual changes bundled into a change presented as flexbox perf work, with the bullet margin removal contradicting the intent that badge position is preserved. Topic header badge alignment and title line height change for all users; since the parent flex container and order context for .extra-info-wrapper are established outside this diff, the accepted 'performance' framing hides that topic-title geometry is being re-tuned here without sign-off.

[BUG] The .panel right-alignment now depends solely on margin-left: auto, which has no equivalent in the legacy -webkit-box/-moz-box/-ms-flexbox display modes the new mixins explicitly emit, so the compat strategy is internally inconsistent. Browsers that resolve the mixin's legacy display declarations (e.g. old Android WebKit receiving display: -webkit-box) do not honor margin-left: auto for right-shifting, so the header panel (user menu/search buttons) renders flush-left/adjacent to the title instead of right-aligned; the previous float: right worked in every mode the mixin targets.

[ADVISORY] The .contents flex conversion is layered on top of the retained .valign-helper mechanism (its rule block is untouched in this diff) even though flex + align-items(center) makes the helper's inline/vertical-align centering trick inert, leaving two competing centering mechanisms in the same container. The next person touching the header must reason about both a dead valign-helper (which, as an inline-block child, still becomes a flex item and can participate in layout) and the flex alignment — the leftover coupling makes the next change riskier and silently preserves a no-op element in markup.

[ADVISORY] @include order(3) on .panel is written against an ordering scheme (orders 1/2 for siblings) that is not defined anywhere in this diff, coupling the header layout to markup/other-file state that is invisible here. If sibling order values live in another file or are expected from future changes, panel position silently depends on a contract with no single source of truth; if they don't exist, order(3) is dead code whose only effect is to move the panel after any later-added default-order(0) sibling — either way the next edit to header children can silently reflow the panel.

[ADVISORY] The new flexbox mixins hardcode an obsolete four-generation vendor-prefix set (including -moz-box and -webkit-box 2009 syntax) as the project-wide fallback strategy, baking a compatibility policy into reusable primitives without any stated browser-support constraint driving it. Every future flexbox call site inherits legacy prefixes that change rendering behavior on legacy engines (as with margin-left:auto and order, which have no -webkit-box equivalent honoring them), so the mixin layer silently guarantees 'flexbox present but semantics differ' rather than a uniform layout — a constraint decision that should be explicit, not emergent from a perf PR.

[ADVISORY] The new flexbox mixins hand-maintain four generations of vendor-prefixed declarations (-webkit-box, -moz-box, -ms-flexbox, -webkit-flex) that duplicate what the build's autoprefixer already emits, creating a parallel hand-updated enumeration of prefix lines per property. Every future flex property added to these mixins (justify-content, flex-wrap, gap...) must be hand-prefixed across the same four legacy syntaxes or it silently never reaches the engines those prefixes target — and the old-box-spec lines (-webkit-box/-moz-box/-webkit-box-align/-moz-box-ordinal-group) are dead for any browser Discourse supports, so each new mixin call ships 3-4 declarations that no engine reads while authors assume they do; the next flexbox change gets riskier and the stylesheets get noisier for no runtime benefit.

[ADVISORY] .valign-helper is retained inside .contents after .contents is converted to a flex container with align-items(center), but its inline-block/vertical-align vertical-centering mechanism no longer participates in a flex layout, leaving inert alignment machinery alongside the new mechanism. The helper still renders as a zero-width flex item in every header, and the next reader or theme author sees two coexisting alignment mechanisms (.valign-helper's vertical-align trick plus align-items:center) and cannot tell which one is load-bearing — changes to one will appear to do nothing because the other or neither is actually controlling layout, making the next header-layout change harder to reason about and debug.

Given those prefixed modes are explicitly part of the mixin’s compat surface, this diff can cause `.panel` to not be pushed to the right edge on those legacy engines, changing/breaking header layout.

This is a plausible, diff-grounded compatibility defect introduced by the change from floats to flex+auto-margins while explicitly targeting legacy implementations.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `.contents` to a flex container and replaces `.panel { float: right; }` with `margin-left: auto` (and adds `order(3)`). That can behave differently under `direction: rtl` / RTL layouts because `float: right` pins to the physical right edge, while flex item placement and the effect of a physical `margin-left: auto` can differ when the flex row is laid out RTL. It is nonetheless a concrete, diff-grounded edge-case concern worth considering (e.g., using logical `margin-inline-start: auto`).
